title: Runs offers pause only where the job machine lets a job go to paused
body:
## Summary
Runs offers pause only where the job machine lets a job go to paused.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Acts.tsx canPause offered pause on planned jobs; jobMachine has no planned->paused edge and kernel job.ts pause refuses it. See commit c655ed60.

## Flow
- seeded red in tests/next-server/runs-console.test.ts or runs-load.test.ts, fixed, re-measured green

## Expected impact
The operator reads acts and counts that agree with what the kernel does. Could break: nothing pinned on the old behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - Runs offers pause only where the job machine lets a job go to paused
Before: 1 of 8 states disagree with the machine (planned)
After: 0 of 8 (canPause reads jobMachine.can)
Method: gate - vitest case red before, green after, with a unit mutant
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A Server Action that rejects leaves Runs with no toast and an unhandled rejection
body:
## Summary
Runs' act runner, the mv send-to-calendar call and the re-route options read chain .then with no .catch: a call that rejects (network gone, server crash before the envelope) shows nothing.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx `run` (void call().then(...).finally(...)), the mv onSchedule `void mv.schedule(...).then(...)`, and the rerouteOptions effect `void port.rerouteOptions(...).then(...)` - 3 sites with no rejection path. runAction wraps body errors into the envelope, so only a transport-level rejection reaches here, and then the operator's press reads as nothing happened. Fixed: each site catches and toasts errorMessage(e) (the options read sets its error).

## Flow
- press P with the dev server stopped
- the Server Action fetch rejects
- busy clears, no toast, console shows an unhandled rejection

## Expected impact
An operator whose act did not reach the server is told so. Could break: nothing; a toast on a path that showed none.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a rejected act is reported
Before: 3 of 3 sites silent on rejection (read)
After: predicted 0 of 3
Method: simulation - the sites are inside a client island; neither the node probe lane (no DOM) nor vitest (no React runtime for effects) witnesses them without extracting the runner
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Runs.tsx run(): void call().then(...).finally(...); onSchedule: void mv.schedule(...).then(...); effect: void port.rerouteOptions(...).then(...)
instrument: extract `run` into a pure act runner in _runs/ (call, toast, refresh) and a vitest case with a rejecting call -> toast called with the rejection's message; red today

title: Runs reads the kernel's jobs twice per render
body:
## Summary
load.ts reads every kernel job with @gt/kernel/job list() and then again through the produce port's listJobs (realRead.jobsView) on every render and every SSE refresh.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/load.ts: `list(store)` (no limit, sliced to KERNEL_CAP after the read) and `port.listJobs()` (jobsView: up to JOBS_CAP=500 parsed, served, priced, scheduled). buildRuns then drops every kernel row the produce read owns (model.ts `owned`). On the real side the produce read covers the same jobs, so the first read pays for rows that are thrown away; on the fixture side the two halves are different universes and both are needed. Fixed: on SIDE=real, skip list() (or read only ids the produce read lacks).

## Flow
- open /projects/runs on the real side with N kernel jobs
- two full jobs-table reads per render

## Expected impact
Runs' render and each live refresh read one jobs table once. Could break: a kernel job the produce read does not serve would vanish if the skip is unconditional.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one jobs read per render
Before: 2 reads of the jobs table per render (read)
After: predicted 1
Method: simulation - no timing harness over a 500-job temp store exists for loadRuns; runs-load.test.ts stubs the stores
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: load.ts: const kj = list(store); ... const pj = port.listJobs(); model.ts: const owned = new Set(produced.map((j) => j.id))
instrument: a vitest over a temp kernel store with 500 jobs counting list()/jobsView reads (or timing loadRuns) on both arms

title: The day-line legend names one state per colour while the colours paint several
body:
## Summary
The legend reads 'at weir' for the amber look, which also paints interrupted jobs, and 'queued' for the idle look, which also paints planned and cancelled.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.tsx LEGEND maps looks to one label; packages/ui/src/components/status/status.ts STATUS.job gives interrupted the 'awaiting' look and planned/cancelled 'idle'. An interrupted job - one whose vendor may have been paid - reads as 'at weir' to an operator who decodes the bar by the legend. Fixed: the legend's labels derived from STATUS.job per look (plus the Weir), or interrupted given its own swatch.

## Flow
- an interrupted kernel job on the day-line
- its bar is amber
- the legend's amber swatch says 'at weir'

## Expected impact
The operator decodes an interrupted bar correctly. Could break: the legend grows; it already hides under 1440 px.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the legend names what each colour paints
Before: 2 of 6 swatches cover states their label does not name (read)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - wording and swatch layout are a design call the round should not make alone; a markup test can pin either answer
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Runs.tsx LEGEND {look:'awaiting', label:'at weir'}, {look:'idle', label:'queued'}; status.ts interrupted: e('awaiting', ...), planned/cancelled: e('idle', ...)
instrument: a markup test: every STATUS.job state's look appears in LEGEND with a label naming it; then cx-capture runs at 1920 to check the legend still fits

title: Runs has no narrow layout: list, day-line and inspector stay three columns
body:
## Summary
Runs.module.css lays .proj as list | main and .runs as day-line | inspector with no breakpoint but the legend's.

## Description
app/(studio)/projects/runs/_runs/Runs.module.css: `.proj{grid-template-columns:var(--w-list) minmax(0,1fr)}`, `.runs{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) var(--w-inspector)}`; the only @media is `(max-width:1440px){.legend{display:none}}`. At phone width the day-line column gets what is left after two fixed columns. Not reproduced this round (no dev server allowed).

## Flow
- cx-capture runs --width 390
- measure the day-line column's width

## Expected impact
Runs is usable on a tablet or phone. Could break: the desktop layout if the breakpoint is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a reproduced viewport
Before: unmeasured (no dev server in a round)
After: predicted: day-line >= 300 px at 390
Method: simulation - cx-capture needs a dev server, which round agents may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: CX_BASE dev server + node pipeline/cx-capture.mjs runs out.png --width 390 on both arms; read the day-line column width
